unresolvedReferences.description: The crown prince whose Eastern Palace was established is not named.
Liu Bao's two elder brothers are unnamed.
Jia, Zou, Mei, and Lu in the Han shu biography title are surnames only and are not resolved to persons.
The Prince of Linchuan (husband of Liu Bao's sister) is referred to only through his consort's title and 王中軍.
The leader of the righteous army (Gaozu) is implicit.
揚、馬、曹、王 and 潘、陸、顏、謝 are surnames of earlier masters; not resolved to individuals.
子建 (Zijian, Cao Zhi's courtesy name) is used figuratively for the addressee; no candidate and not captured as a separate person.
兩唐 ('two Tang') is obscure; the packet's 'two Tang histories' is doubtful and left unrepaired.
The Chu song quoted ('They named me Zhengze') is from the Li Sao (Qu Yuan), who is not named here.
平原兄弟 ('the Pingyuan brothers') is not resolved to specific persons.
三張二陸兩潘一左 are collective surname groups of Taikang poets, not individually named.
The emperor issuing the edict (Gaozu) is implicit.
The mysterious stranger at the inn who prophesied Zhou Xingsi's career is unnamed.
虞騫 is Yu Qian; chunk 003 (s0198) rendered the same man as 'Yu Xie' following the packet English.
